app.name: Instagram
app.description: A free photo and video sharing app from Meta with feeds, Stories, Reels, and direct messaging, used by over 2 billion people worldwide.

verdict.one_liner: Instagram shows you ads using everything it knows about you, including where you go, what you search, and how you behave, and it can read your direct messages.
verdict.summary: Instagram is an ad-supported platform owned by Meta. It collects extensive data including your precise location, contacts, browsing history, search history, device fingerprints, and behavior patterns to target ads. Unlike WhatsApp, standard direct messages are not end-to-end encrypted, meaning Meta can access their contents. The app tracks you across third-party apps and websites. While some ad controls exist, opting out of tracking entirely is not practical for most users.
verdict.recommendation_reason: If you value message privacy and want to avoid behavioral tracking for ads, consider alternatives like Signal for messaging or apps with stronger privacy commitments.

red.title: Your direct messages are not end-to-end encrypted
red.plain_english: Unlike WhatsApp, standard direct messages on Instagram are not end-to-end encrypted. Meta can read the contents of your DMs if required by law or for moderation purposes.

red.title: Your behavior powers ads across the internet
red.plain_english: Instagram tracks what you do inside the app and on other websites and apps, then uses this to show you targeted ads. This includes your searches, browsing history, and how you interact with posts.

red.title: Your exact location is collected and used for ads
red.plain_english: Instagram collects both your precise GPS location and your approximate location from your IP address. This location data is used to target ads and recommend local content.

red.title: Deep device fingerprinting linked across Meta apps
red.plain_english: Instagram collects your device model, operating system, unique device identifiers, and app usage patterns. These identifiers are linked across all Meta apps you use, creating a detailed profile of you.

red.title: Your contacts are uploaded to find friends
red.plain_english: If you allow contact access, Instagram uploads the phone numbers in your address book to its servers to suggest people you may know. This includes people who never agreed to share their information.

green.title: You can request that your data be deleted
green.plain_english: Instagram provides a way to download a copy of your data and to request account deletion. Once deleted, your profile and posts are removed from public view.

green.title: Data is encrypted in transit
green.plain_english: Your data is transferred over secure HTTPS connections when you use the app, which prevents outsiders from intercepting it on the network.

green.title: Some ad personalization controls are available
green.plain_english: You can limit some ad targeting in your Instagram settings, such as turning off ads based on data from partners. However, this does not stop all tracking.

categories.label: Camera & Microphone
categories.plain_english: Instagram only uses your camera and microphone when you actively take a photo, record a video, go live, or make a voice/video call. It does not listen or record in the background.
categories.detail: Camera and microphone access are user-initiated for Stories, Reels, posts, Live, and calls. The App Store privacy label confirms access is on-demand and not continuous.
categories.policy_excerpt: Camera and microphone are accessed only when you choose to create or share content, or during an active call.
concerns: No end-to-end encryption on standard video/voice calls within the app

categories.label: Location & GPS
categories.plain_english: Instagram collects your precise GPS location when you tag a post or use location features, and it always estimates your rough location from your IP address to target ads and recommend local content.
categories.detail: The App Store privacy label lists both 'Precise Location' and 'Coarse Location' as collected. Precise location is optional and user-initiated for geo-tagging posts and location-based features. Coarse location is continuously inferred from IP address and used for ad targeting, content recommendations, and diagnostics. There is no opt-out for IP-based location inference.
categories.policy_excerpt: Location data is collected when you use location-related features and is also inferred from your IP address for various purposes including ads and recommendations.
concerns: Precise location collected and used for advertising
IP-based location inference is always on with no opt-out
Location data flows to Meta's advertising systems

categories.label: Contacts & Phonebook
categories.plain_english: If you choose to allow it, Instagram uploads the phone numbers from your address book to suggest friends. This includes people who do not use Instagram and never agreed to have their data shared.
categories.detail: Contact syncing is optional but encouraged during onboarding. The uploaded contact list is stored on Meta servers and used to build social connection recommendations. The App Store label lists 'Contacts' as collected. There is no indication that this data is isolated from Meta's broader data infrastructure.
categories.policy_excerpt: If you choose to sync your contacts, we collect the phone numbers in your address book to help you find people you know on Instagram.
concerns: Non-users' phone numbers uploaded without their consent
Contact data likely shared within Meta's advertising systems
No clear retention policy for non-user contact numbers

categories.label: Storage & File Access
categories.plain_english: Instagram only accesses your photos and videos when you choose to post them, add to your story, or send in a message. It does not scan your camera roll in the background.
categories.detail: Storage access is user-initiated for posting content to the feed, Stories, Reels, or sending via direct message. The App Store label lists 'Photos or Videos' as collected. There is no indication of background library scanning.
categories.policy_excerpt: You can choose to share photos and videos from your device when creating posts, stories, or sending messages.

categories.label: Data Sharing with 3rd Parties
categories.plain_english: Instagram shares your data extensively with other Meta companies and uses it to track you across third-party apps and websites for advertising. Your contact info, identifiers, and other data are linked with data from outside Instagram.
categories.detail: The App Store privacy label explicitly lists 'Data Used to Track You' across third-party apps and sites, including Contact Info, Identifiers, and Other Data. Data is also 'Linked to You' for Third-Party Advertising. The Play Store Data Safety notes 'Device or other IDs' are shared with other companies for 'Advertising or marketing.' Meta's privacy policy confirms intra-family data sharing for ads and product improvement. The scope includes behavioral, device, location, and account data.
categories.policy_excerpt: We share information with other Meta Companies to help provide, improve, and promote Meta Company Products, including for ads and products experience across those platforms.
concerns: Cross-app tracking across third-party apps and websites
Device IDs shared with other companies for advertising
Extensive intra-Meta data sharing for ad targeting
No meaningful opt-out from tracking for most users

categories.label: Account & Identity Data
categories.plain_english: You must give Instagram your real email address, phone number, and name to create an account. Your profile information is public by default, and your account can be linked to your Facebook profile through Meta's Accounts Center.
categories.detail: An email address or phone number is required for registration. The App Store label lists extensive contact info collected: physical address, email, name, phone number, and other user contact info. Profile name, photo, and bio are visible to other users by default. Meta's Accounts Center allows linking Instagram to Facebook and WhatsApp, creating a unified identity profile.
categories.policy_excerpt: We collect the content, communications, and other information you provide when you use our Products, including when you sign up for an account.
concerns: Real identity required — anonymous use not possible
Profile data public by default
Account linkable to Facebook for unified ad profile

categories.label: Behavioural & Ad Tracking
categories.plain_english: Instagram's entire business model is based on tracking your behavior to show you ads. It records your searches, browsing history, which posts you tap, how long you watch videos, and what you buy, then uses this to target ads at you both inside and outside the app.
categories.detail: The App Store label lists 'Browsing History', 'Search History', 'Usage Data' (Product Interaction, Advertising Data, Other Usage Data), and 'Sensitive Info' as collected and linked to identity for advertising, analytics, and personalization. Instagram shows ads in the feed, Stories, Reels, and Explore. It also tracks user behavior across third-party apps and sites using Meta's advertising SDKs and pixels. This is comprehensive behavioral profiling.
categories.policy_excerpt: We collect information about how you use our Products, such as the types of content you view or engage with, the features you use, the actions you take, and the time, frequency, and duration of your activities.
concerns: Browsing history and search history collected for ads
Cross-app and cross-site behavioral tracking
Ad targeting based on sensitive inferences
No way to use the app without behavioral tracking

categories.label: Children's Data Handling
categories.plain_english: Instagram says you must be at least 13 years old to use the app. However, there is no real age verification — you just enter a birth date. Some Instagram content and features are designed to appeal to younger teens.
categories.detail: The Terms of Service require users to be 13 or older. There is no robust age verification mechanism beyond self-reported birth date. Instagram offers some teen safety features (like default private accounts for under-18s in some regions), but the platform's design and content are broadly appealing to children and young teens.
categories.policy_excerpt: You must be at least 13 years old to create an account on Instagram.
concerns: No age verification beyond self-attestation
Platform design and content appeal to younger audiences
Extensive data collection on teens for ad targeting

categories.label: Network & Internet Activity
categories.plain_english: Instagram always logs your IP address when you use the app and uses it to estimate your general location for security, diagnostics, and ad targeting. This happens every time you open the app.
categories.detail: IP address logging is continuous during app use. The IP is used for approximate location inference (city/country level), security monitoring, and diagnostic purposes. The App Store label lists 'Other Data' used for tracking, which includes IP-derived information. There is no opt-out for IP-based logging.
categories.policy_excerpt: We collect information from and about the computers, phones, and other web-connected devices you use that integrate with our Products.
concerns: IP-based location inference always on with no opt-out
Connection metadata logged continuously

categories.label: Device Info & Fingerprinting
categories.plain_english: Instagram collects detailed information about your device including its model, operating system, unique device IDs, and app performance data. These identifiers are shared across all Meta apps to link your activity together.
categories.detail: The App Store label lists 'Identifiers' (User ID, Device ID) and 'Diagnostics' (Crash Data, Performance Data, Other Diagnostic Data) as collected. Meta's privacy policy explicitly collects device attributes including hardware model, OS version, battery level, signal strength, carrier, and unique identifiers. These device IDs enable cross-app tracking within the Meta ecosystem.
categories.policy_excerpt: We collect device attributes such as operating system, hardware and software versions, battery level, signal strength, available storage space, browser type, app and file names and types, and plugins.
concerns: Device IDs explicitly linked across all Meta products
Diagnostic data collected beyond what is needed for service operation
Enables re-identification across separate Meta accounts

categories.label: Health & Biometric Data
categories.plain_english: The App Store privacy label says Instagram may optionally collect health and fitness data. If you use biometric unlock like Face ID, that data stays on your phone and Instagram never sees it.
categories.detail: The App Store label lists 'Health & Fitness' data (Health, Fitness) as collected for Analytics and App Functionality. This suggests optional health-related features may collect such data. Device-level biometric authentication (Face ID, Touch ID) is handled by the operating system locally and is not accessed by Instagram.
categories.policy_excerpt: Health and fitness data may be collected for optional features.
concerns: Health data collection purpose is vague in disclosures
Optional does not mean clearly disclosed to users at point of collection

categories.label: Financial & Payment Data
categories.plain_english: Instagram collects your purchase history and some financial information if you make purchases through the app or connect payment methods. This data is used for analytics and to process transactions.
categories.detail: The App Store label lists 'Purchases' (Purchase History) and 'Financial Info' (Other Financial Info, Payment Info, Credit Info) as collected. Instagram has in-app shopping, tipping, and paid promotion features. Payment processing is handled by third-party processors for some transactions, but purchase history and financial info are collected by Instagram.
categories.policy_excerpt: If you use our Products for purchases or other financial transactions, we collect information about the purchase or transaction.
concerns: Purchase history used for ad targeting and profiling
Financial data scope is broad in App Store disclosures

categories.label: Data Deletion & User Rights
categories.plain_english: You can download a copy of your Instagram data and request to delete your account. However, some data may be kept for legal or safety reasons, and content you shared with others remains visible on their accounts even after you delete yours.
categories.detail: Instagram provides 'Download Your Information' and 'Delete Your Account' features. Account deletion removes the profile and posts from public view. However, messages sent to others remain in their inboxes, comments on others' posts persist, and some data may be retained for legal compliance, safety, or integrity purposes. The Play Store Data Safety confirms 'You can request that data be deleted.'
categories.policy_excerpt: You can delete your account at any time. When you delete your account, we delete things you have posted, such as your photos and videos.
concerns: Data shared with others (messages, comments) is not deleted from their accounts
Some retention for legal/safety purposes is not time-limited
Account deletion is not instantaneous in all systems

categories.label: Policy Change Notification
categories.plain_english: If Instagram changes its privacy policy, it will update the effective date and may notify you. But by continuing to use the app, you automatically accept the new terms without having to actively agree.
categories.detail: Meta's Terms of Service state that continued use of the service constitutes acceptance of updated terms. Users who disagree must delete their account. There is no mechanism for selectively accepting or rejecting specific changes, and no requirement for active re-consent.
categories.policy_excerpt: We will notify you before we make changes to these terms and give you the opportunity to review the revised terms before continuing to use our Products.
concerns: Passive acceptance by continued use — no active re-consent required
No granular opt-out for specific policy changes
